cues.en: So the competition for C back in the early to mid 1970s as a system programming language was...

cues.zh: Pascal？！真有人认真提议把 Pascal 当作系统编程语言。
cues.en: Pascal?! People seriously suggested Pascal as a system programming language.

cues.zh: Pascal 有很多优点，但是……系统编程？开什么玩笑。
cues.en: Pascal had lots of good things about it, but... system programming? It's a joke.

cues.zh: 你根本不可能用它做这个。所以那只是个例子。
cues.en: You couldn't possibly do it in that. So that was an example.

cues.zh: 哦，还有 C 的另一个竞争对手，在那个小光谱的另一端，
cues.en: Oh, and the other competition for C, at sort of the other end of that little spectrum,

cues.zh: 是无类型的语言，比如 BCPL，它其实非常优雅，
cues.en: was languages that were typeless, like BCPL, which was really elegant,

cues.zh: 但无类型语言：和当时机器的架构不匹配。所以，竞争很弱。
cues.en: but typeless language: didn't match the architecture of the machines at the time. So, weak competition.

cues.zh: 想想浏览器上的 Javascript 和 Java。
cues.en: Think about Javascript, versus Java, on browsers.

cues.zh: Java 先到了，但不是那种正确的竞争方式。
cues.en: Java got there first, but wasn't the right kind of competition.

cues.zh: Javascript 做得更好，因为人们把 Javascript 源代码发送到浏览器要容易得多，
cues.en: Javascript did better, because it was enormously easier for people to send Javascript source code to a browser,

cues.zh: 而不必先编译，再把编译结果发送到浏览器。
cues.en: rather than having to compile something and then send the compiled result to the browser.

cues.zh: 所以 Java 在浏览器端其实一直没真正流行起来，JavaScript 始终在那里胜出。
cues.en: So Java never took off, really, on the browser side of things; Javascript always won there.

cues.zh: 运气好确实有帮助。C 在时机上运气很好，它伴随着小型机一起出现。
cues.en: It helps to have good luck. C had good luck in timing. It came along with minicomputers.

cues.zh: 后来它又随着工作站迎来了一波新的生机，想想 Sun 的工作站。
cues.en: Then it got a new burst of life with workstations; think of the Sun workstations.

cues.zh: 接着它又随着 PC 迎来了一波，然后又随着嵌入式系统迎来了一波。
cues.en: And then it got another burst with the PC. And then it got another burst with embedded systems.

cues.zh: 所以 C 长期以来一直在冲浪，每次都能借到新的顺风。
cues.en: So C has kind of been surfing the wave for a long time, getting that fresh wind each time.

cues.zh: 想想 Objective-C，如果你能想到的话。Objective-C……
cues.en: Think of Objective C, if you can. Objective C...

cues.zh: 有点像 C++，但不是长得像，那种说法不对——
cues.en: kind of a C++, not look-alike, that's the wrong characterization --

cues.zh: 但是，你知道，它试图在同一个领域竞争，基本没怎么被用。
cues.en: but, you know, attempting to compete in the same space, pretty much unused.

cues.zh: 后来它被 Steve Jobs 选中，在 NeXT 工作站上运行，然后
cues.en: And then it was picked up to run on the NeXT Workstation, by Steve Jobs, and then

cues.zh: 被带进了 Apple，在那里被用了很长时间（而且显然现在还在用，
cues.en: carried into Apple, where it was used for a very long time (and still is,

cues.zh: 用来为 MacOSX 开发软件，某种程度上也为 iOS 开发。
cues.en: obviously) to create software for MacOSX, and, to some extent, iOS.

cues.zh: Swift 出现后会发生什么？我觉得 Swift 大概……你可以纠正我，
cues.en: What's going to happen when Swift comes along? I think Swift is probably... you can correct me,

cues.zh: 我觉得它可能会在未来——随便挑个时间段——5 到 10 年内终结 Objective C。
cues.en: I think probably going to be the death of Objective C over the next --

cues.zh: 我不确定，
cues.en: pick a time period -- 5 or 10 years. I don't know for sure,

cues.zh: 但我猜情况可能就是这样。
cues.en: but I will guess that might be the case.

cues.zh: 不过 Objective C 的成功当时靠的是运气，你知道，就是恰好在正确的时间出现在正确的地点，
cues.en: But the success of Objective C, and then, was luck, you know, just being in the right place at the right time

cues.zh: 或许吧，然后我觉得它的消亡，大概是因为它的细分领域会消失。
cues.en: perhaps, and then I think its death will be its niche probably goes away.

cues.zh: 我也不知道这些东西在新语言上会怎么发展，比如我前面提到的 Rust、Go 或 Dart。
cues.en: And I don't know how any of this stuff will work on new languages, like Rust, or Go, or Dart, which I mentioned earlier.

cues.zh: 那语言为什么会失败？嗯，我已经告诉过你一些答案了。
cues.en: And then why do languages fail? Well, I already told you some of the answers.

cues.zh: 领域消失了。很多 Troff 相关的工具就是这样。
cues.en: The domain disappears. That's what happened to a lot of the Troff-related tools.

cues.zh: 就这么——它已经消失了。工程实现可能有问题：语言太大，或者太复杂。
cues.en: Just -- it's gone away. The engineering might be bad: languages are too big, or too complicated.

cues.zh: Algol-68 就是一个绝佳的例子，出自英国。
cues.en: Algol-68 is a wonderful example produced in the United Kingdom.

cues.zh: PL/1 也是一个绝佳的例子，出自美国。
cues.en: PL/1 is a wonderful example produced in the United States.

cues.zh: 太大、太慢、太晚、太复杂——诸如此类的问题。
cues.en: Too big, too slow, too late, too complicated -- all kinds of things like that.

cues.zh: 那 Perl 6 呢？我们会说它“太晚”了吗？
cues.en: What about Perl 6? We would call that "too late"?

cues.zh: 我们大概会说它太晚了。我觉得 Perl 的时代已经过去了，
cues.en: We would probably call that too late. I think Perl's time has passed,

cues.zh: 因为它在某种意义上已经停止演进了，而 Perl 6 永远不会真正到来——
cues.en: because it's stopped evolving in some sense, and Perl 6 is never going to arrive, really --

cues.zh: 所以 Perl 在某种意义上错过了一班船。是不是永久错过，我不知道；它仍然是一门非常有用的语言，
cues.en: and so Perl's, in some sense, missed a boat. Permanently, I don't know; it's still a very useful language,

cues.zh: 但接下来会怎样，倒是挺值得看的。
cues.en: but that will be interesting to see what happens.

cues.zh: 那 C++ 呢？太大？大得可怕？复杂得可怕？它会消失吗？
cues.en: How about C++? Too big? Awfully big? Awfully complicated? Is it going to go away?

cues.zh: 大概不会，因为嵌入式基础还在。外面有大量 C++ 代码，人们也在写
cues.en: Probably not because the embedded base. There's an awful lot of C++ code out there, and people are writing

cues.zh: 不少新东西。但你会想，它是不是已经越过了某个复杂度阈值，
cues.en: a fair amount of new stuff. But you wonder whether it's passed some threshold of

cues.zh: 到了凡人、至少普通人难以企及的地步。
cues.en: complexity that's beyond mortals, at least ordinary people.

cues.zh: 然后还有哲学选择层面的问题。有些语言把意识形态推得有点过头了。
cues.en: And then there's questions of the sort of philosophical choices. Some languages take ideology a little too far.

cues.zh: 某种程度上是往函数式语言那边。很多人——尤其是我——
cues.en: to functional languages in some sense. A lot of people -- me, in particular --

cues.zh: 并不是以函数式程序员所需的那种数学严谨、抽象的方式思考的。
cues.en: do not think in the sort of mathematically rigorous and abstract way that you need to be

cues.zh: 所以，谁知道呢。
cues.en: a functional programmer. So, who knows.

cues.zh: 语言可能失败的原因有很多。
cues.en: Lots of different reasons why languages potentially fail.

cues.zh: 不过我觉得很少有语言会彻底消失。所以我才说“未能繁荣”。
cues.en: Now I think very few languages ever disappear totally. So that's why I said "fail to thrive".

cues.zh: 它们并没有消失，只是不再增长了。而且它们的用户群在萎缩。
cues.en: They don't disappear; it's just that they don't grow. And their user population shrinks.

cues.zh: 最后，我用 Alan Perlis 的一句评论来收尾，这话绝对正确。
cues.en: Let me close with an observation from Alan Perlis, which is absolutely true.

cues.zh: 我不在乎你用什么语言；你都能写出烂代码——这大概就是他那句话的另一种说法。
cues.en: I don't care what your language is; you can write lousy code - which is, I guess, another way of what he said.

cues.zh: 但这给我的启示是，还有非常非常非常大的空间
cues.en: But what it suggests to me is that there is still lots and lots and lots of room

cues.zh: 去动手发明、创造新语言，在某种意义上
cues.en: for going off and inventing, creating new languages that in some sense

cues.zh: 尝试把前人最好的东西结合起来，但又有一些新的诠释
cues.en: try to combine the best stuff from what went before, but have some new take on it

cues.zh: 让它在某种程度上变得有趣、变得更好。
cues.en: that makes it interesting and better in some sort of way.

cues.zh: “太数学化”这顶帽子，我想，你或许可以说
cues.en: The "too mathematical" brush, you could, I suppose, arguably apply

cues.zh: 所以如果你想做这件事，大概应该从领域特定语言入手，
cues.en: So probably if you want to do this, the place to start is with domain-specific languages,

cues.zh: 而不是大型通用语言。别去造下一个 C++，
cues.en: rather than big general-purpose ones. Don't build the next C++,

cues.zh: 而是去造下一个——我也不知道，正则表达式——
cues.en: but build the next -- I don't know, regular expressions --

cues.zh: 你知道，造点小东西。
cues.en: you know, something small.

cues.zh: 你可能会发现这特别有趣，
cues.en: And you might discover that it's an enormous amount of fun,

cues.zh: 你可能会对事情产生影响，这确实非常有满足感。
cues.en: and that you might have an effect on things, and it's certainly very satisfying.

cues.zh: 总之，我想说的就这些。再次非常感谢你们的热情款待
cues.en: So, anyway, that's all I wanted to say. Thank you again very much for your hospitality

cues.zh: 和关注。我真的很感激。[掌声]
cues.en: and your attention. I really appreciate it. [applause]
